service.name: Client dinner and member event entertainment
service.serviceType: Live music for client dinners, member events and private clubs
service.description: Jazz duo and small ensembles for client dinners, member events and private clubs in Denver, played at conversation volume with every rate published.

faqs.q: How loud is a jazz duo during dinner?
faqs.a: Dinner and cocktail sets run 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table, a level you can talk across without raising your voice. If your venue or club enforces a cap, give us the number at contract and the evening is built under it rather than argued about on the night.

faqs.q: What does music for a client dinner cost?
faqs.a: The jazz duo prices by the hour, and both the hourly figure and the cocktails-and-dinner range are published on this page and on the rate card. There is no overtime rate: added time bills at the same hourly figure in 30-minute increments, agreed on the night with whoever holds the budget.

faqs.q: Can you invoice against a purchase order?
faqs.a: Yes. We can be set up as a vendor, quote against a PO, and invoice net-30 on approval, with the purchase order number on one itemised invoice. The certificate of insurance naming your venue and the W-9 arrive in the same email as the contract, before anyone has to ask for them.

faqs.q: Does the music stop for toasts and remarks?
faqs.a: Yes, before the speaker reaches the microphone. A dedicated announcement microphone is live on its own channel from the end of sound check, so toasts, introductions and remarks get a working mic of their own rather than the singer's. Transitions are set against your run of show before the event.

faqs.q: How much space does the duo need?
faqs.a: An 8 by 6 foot corner, one dedicated 20-amp circuit, and a 60-minute load-in. No stage and no house sound system are required: sound sized to the venue is included in the rate, and the footprint for every size up to quartet is published on the technical page.
